The Federal Open Market Committee of the Federal Reserve (the Fed) announced earlier today (Hong Kong time) its decision to keep the target range for the federal funds rate unchanged at 3.75-4%.

The policy decision is in line with market expectations. The statement released after the meeting indicated that economic activity was expanding at a strong pace and the labour market was stable, but inflation has remained elevated. This reflects that the Committee is watchful over the outlook on inflation, though it may need more time to observe how the data evolves.

Hong Kong’s monetary and financial markets have continued to operate in an orderly manner. As the noticeable HKD-USD interest rate differential persists, carry trade activities may cause the Hong Kong dollar to gradually ease. That said, the outlook for the Hong Kong dollar and interbank rates can vary due to various factors, such as the market’s risk appetite for carry trades, and the supply-demand conditions for Hong Kong dollars which are in turn influenced by capital market activities and other seasonal factors.

US interest rate adjustments are subject to considerable uncertainty, and will depend on developments in inflation, labour market, and other economic data, and may influence the interest rate environment in Hong Kong.

The public should carefully manage interest rate risks when making decisions about property purchase, investment or borrowing.

Upon the USM implementation of the USM on 16 November 2026, the scrip fee concession will cease to apply, and the stock withdrawal fee concession scheme will be updated to align with the revised fee structure and operational arrangements under the USM.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced today (15 October) the “ART” Framework to support the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (A.I.) in the banking sector, fostering an A.I.-enabled banking ecosystem with Accountability, Resilience, and Trust.

A.I. systems are becoming more autonomous, with greater access to data, tools and workflows. With the aim of supporting banks in seizing the opportunities presented by A.I. while maintaining robust governance and operational resilience, key initiatives under the “ART” Framework include:

Issued the latest Supervisory Guidance for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence, drawing on insights from the second cohort of the Generative A.I. (GenA.I.) Sandbox1;

Further testing of agentic A.I. applications through the GenA.I. Sandbox++2 and an upcoming discussion paper on a proposed supervisory framework for agentic A.I. governance, exploring intent-anchored accountability, a registry of material A.I. agents, and effective intervention mechanisms.

Mr Arthur Yuen, Deputy Chief Executive of the HKMA, said, “The progression from generative to agentic A.I. represents an important new stage of innovation for the banking sector.

Under Fintech 20303, the HKMA is introducing the ‘ART’ Framework, which stands for Accountability, Resiliency and Trust, with the aim of providing a clear foundation for banks to develop and deploy A.I. responsibly.

The HKMA is also co-hosting the two-day “Finance + A.I.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), as representative of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government (HKSAR Government), announced today (14 October) that a tender of 10-year HKD institutional Government Bonds (Bonds) through the re-opening of existing 10-year Government Bond issue 10GB3507001 under the Infrastructure Bond Programme will be held on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, for settlement on Thursday, 22 October 2026.

An additional amount of HK$1.25 billion of the outstanding 10-year Bonds (issue no. 10GB3507001) will be on offer. Tender is open only to Primary Dealers appointed under the Infrastructure Bond Programme. Anyone wishing to apply for the Bonds on offer can do so through any of the Primary Dealers on the latest published list, which can be obtained from the Hong Kong Government Bonds website at https://www.hkgb.gov.hk. Each tender must be for an amount of HK$50,000 or integral multiples thereof.

Tender results will be published on the HKMA’s website, the Hong Kong Government Bonds website, Bloomberg (GBHK <GO>) and Refinitiv (IBPGSBPINDEX). The publication time is expected to be no later than 3:00 pm on the tender day.

The Chongqing and Hong Kong authorities announced today (14 October) the launch of the Chongqing-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform (CQ-HK DVP).

As set out in “The Chief Executive’s 2026 Policy Address”, this new cross-boundary data validation mechanism jointly established with Chongqing is one of the measures for encouraging the orderly flow of financial elements between the Chinese Mainland and Hong Kong. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) facilitated the establishment of the CQ-HK DVP1 together with authorities including the People’s Bank of China Chongqing Municipal Branch, the Office of the Financial Commission of the Chongqing Municipal Committee, the Office of the Cyberspace Affairs Commission of the Chongqing Municipal Committee, and the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the Chongqing Municipal People’s Government.

Leveraging blockchain technology and data coding (i.e. hash values), the CQ-HK DVP enables the verification of data presented by customers without involving the cross-boundary transfer or storage of the original documents. The relevant innovative technologies and mechanism have been successfully applied and proven to be stable and effective via the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Cross-boundary Data Validation Platform2.

The CQ-HK DVP will mainly support cross-boundary financial use cases at the outset.

The CQ-HK DVP will further foster secure and efficient cross-boundary data flow between Chongqing and Hong Kong.
